issue_context.summary: Universal tab switching across Explorer, browsers, and Terminal exceeds Window Hopper's top-level HWND model and lacks a selected application integration contract.
known_information: Window Hopper switches separate top-level windows within the current application.
Requested tabs live inside one application window.
Different applications expose tabs through different shortcuts, accessibility trees, or private extension APIs.
inferences: A universal implementation would require per-application adapters or a deliberately limited accessibility contract, not a small extension of HWND enumeration.
issue_context.analysis: The user scenario is valid, but the issue does not define a product boundary that can be designed and tested as one feature. The useful maintainer action is to explain the integration choice required.
initial_investigation: src/modules/AltWindowCycle/AltWindowCycle.cpp gathers and filters top-level HWND candidates.
The current module has no browser, Explorer, or Terminal tab-provider abstraction.
No assigned owner or linked implementation appears on the issue.

actions.label: Post Window Hopper scope response

comment.body: Window Hopper currently operates on top-level application windows. The requested tabs belong to different applications—Explorer, browsers, and Terminal—and do not share one universal enumeration and activation contract, so system-wide tab support is substantially broader than extending the existing window list. This should not enter implementation as one generic Window Hopper change; maintainers would first need to select a specific supported application/API or define a separate app-integration model. Each application's native tab shortcut remains the reliable path today.
